lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Supervised application: keeping records that make a dispute winnable

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic keeping records that make a dispute winnable task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: With a trusted adult's help, the learner finds two real documents already kept in the household (paper or digital) and logs, for each, what it proves, its date, and where it's stored, leaving out any account number, card number, or password entirely.
safetyNotes: No account number, card number, password, or full financial detail is ever written into the log; only what the document proves, its date, and its storage location are recorded.
A trusted adult identifies which real household documents are appropriate to use for this exercise before the learner handles them.
If no adult is available or no suitable document exists in the household right now, use the alternative below instead.

simulationAlternative.description: If no real document is available or supervision isn't possible right now, the learner instead uses the two fictional sample documents from an earlier lesson this unit and builds the same documentation log entries for those instead.

materials: learner-local: a notebook or document for the log

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l04-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: What would make you actually keep a log like this going forward, rather than doing it once for this lesson?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g10-u04-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Log completeness: Both entries include all three fields. | Privacy discipline: No sensitive number or password appears in the log. | Understanding of dispute usefulness: Explains a specific, plausible way the log entry would help in a dispute. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner set up one simple ongoing habit (a folder, a note, or a recurring reminder) for logging new documents like these as they come in, and describe exactly how it will work.

duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

resources.title: keeping records that make a dispute winnable worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: With a trusted adult's help, the learner finds two real documents already kept in the household (paper or digital) and logs, for each, what it proves, its date, and where it's stored, leaving out any account number, card number, or password entirely.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact keeping records that make a dispute winnable decision or action.
Model move 2: With your adult, choose two real documents already kept in the household that would be useful in a dispute.
Model move 3: For each document, log what it proves, its date, and where it's stored.

Model check: Log completeness: Both entries include all three fields. | Privacy discipline: No sensitive number or password appears in the log. | Understanding of dispute usefulness: Explains a specific, plausible way the log entry would help in a dispute.

resources.title: keeping records that make a dispute winnable action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for keeping records that make a dispute winnable.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: keeping records that make a dispute winnable coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: With a trusted adult's help, the learner finds two real documents already kept in the household (paper or digital) and logs, for each, what it proves, its date, and where it's stored, leaving out any account number, card number, or password entirely.
Coach direction: With your adult, choose two real documents already kept in the household that would be useful in a dispute.
Learner prompt: Briefly describe, in general terms, what kind of documents you chose (for example, 'a repair confirmation' or 'a receipt'), without any account or card numbers.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: keeping records that make a dispute winnable complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: For each document, log what it proves, its date, and where it's stored.
Response 1 (t2-p1): My log entries name what each document proves and its date.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My log entries name where each document is stored, so it could be found again later.
Response 3 (t2-p3): No account number, card number, or password appears anywhere in my log.

Equal-access rule: If no real document is available or supervision isn't possible right now, the learner instead uses the two fictional sample documents from an earlier lesson this unit and builds the same documentation log entries for those instead.

resources.title: keeping records that make a dispute winnable minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: What would make you actually keep a log like this going forward, rather than doing it once for this lesson?

Success checks: Log completeness: Both entries include all three fields. | Privacy discipline: No sensitive number or password appears in the log. | Understanding of dispute usefulness: Explains a specific, plausible way the log entry would help in a dispute.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: keeping records that make a dispute winnable supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g10-u04-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional keeping records that make a dispute winnable condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Log completeness: Both entries include all three fields. | Privacy discipline: No sensitive number or password appears in the log. | Understanding of dispute usefulness: Explains a specific, plausible way the log entry would help in a dispute..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.
